festivals.name: Daisy Chain Fields (Olivia Rodrigo)
festivals.location: Great Park Live, Irvine (OC — ~45 mi, worth the drive)
festivals.why: Olivia Rodrigo's first festival — a one-day, all-women lineup (Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, The Breeders, Bikini Kill, Garbage, Santigold + special guests Stevie Nicks, Karen O, Sarah McLachlan), 100% of net proceeds to women/girls nonprofits. Off the core house/techno lane, but a marquee must-know — and squarely on-taste for the Lori profile (she tracks Olivia Rodrigo + Mitski). Sold out; only path in now is the L.A. Works volunteer-drive ticket lottery (125 pairs) or resale.

festivals.name: CRSSD Festival — Fall 2026
festivals.why: SD is a drive, but this is festival-tier and on-taste — Disclosure, Chris Lake, Groove Armada (DJ set), Helena Hauff, Ben UFO, I Hate Models, Mathame, Carlita, salute. House/ techno/melodic, European lean, waterfront, 21+. NOTE: same weekend as Portola (SF) — can't do both; pick one.

festivals.name: Portola 2026
festivals.why: THE one for you — electronic-forward with DESPACIO (James Murphy + 2ManyDJs sound system), Four Tet, Soulwax, Groove Armada, DJ Shadow, Fatboy Slim, Skepta, plus Robyn, Tiësto, Swedish House Mafia. European/house energy in a warehouse-pier setting. 2-day ~$380.

festivals.name: Coachella 2027
festivals.why: Advance GA already sold out (~$549–599); lineup typically drops Sept 2026–Jan 2027. Worth tracking the lineup announce to decide if a resale is worth it.

festivals.name: GALA Festival (London) — 2027 edition
festivals.why: Quintessential European house/disco day-fest (2026: Seth Troxler, Todd Terje, Call Super, DJ Seinfeld). On-taste, but not timely — only bubble up when 2027 presale/lineup drops.

dining.name: Mírate
dining.notes: Multi-level rooftop, Tulum-jungle candlelight; bar voted Best in California. Strong chic/date-night + birthday pick. Eastside.

dining.name: Wilde's
dining.notes: Tiny candlelit British bistro/wine bar; bakery-cafe by day. Intimate date-night; tables hard — Notify/bar seats. Eastside.

dining.name: Cafe Stella
dining.notes: Reopened after 2024 closure; slimmed menu — steak au poivre, frisée, frozen-lemon sorbet. Sunset Junction, home turf.

dining.name: Rasarumah
dining.notes: Eastside hotspot (Variety also flagged it). Confirm exact address/neighborhood next pass.

dining.name: Dunsmoor
dining.notes: Restored 1920s building around a huge wood-burning hearth. Eastside, on-profile for a special night.

dining.name: Yess
dining.notes: Grew out of the Yess Aquatic seafood truck. Chef Junya Yamasaki — confirm details next pass.

dining.name: Sushi Nakazawa
dining.notes: Omakase from a Jiro Ono protégé; NYC import's LA debut. Neighborhood unconfirmed.

dining.name: Hermon's
dining.notes: Refreshed chophouse from the Found Oyster team — martinis, pull-apart garlic bread, pasta vongole. Confirm neighborhood.

dining.name: Mish
dining.notes: New-wave deli on La Brea — wood-fired bagels, shakshuka with challah, pastrami reuben on schmaltz-griddled rye.

dining.name: Asadero
dining.notes: Above-average taco stand — smoky asada from a chef who left corporate kitchens. Confirm neighborhood.

dining.name: Amiguita
dining.notes: On the Resy Hit List; details unconfirmed — fill in cuisine/neighborhood next pass.

dining.name: Pasjoli
dining.notes: Refined French bistro, Chef Dave Beran (ex-Alinea). Westside — special-occasion, not walkable.

dining.name: Kassi
dining.notes: Greek-Med rooftop in Venice — mezze, lamb chops, grilled whole fish. Westside.

dining.name: San Laurel
dining.notes: Spanish-inflected dining high in the InterContinental DTLA (José Andrés group).

dining.name: Calabra
dining.notes: Mediterranean rooftop atop the Santa Monica Proper — charred flatbreads, mezze, grilled fish.

dining.name: Found Oyster
dining.notes: Tiny, buzzy seafood bar — clam cakes, chicken-fried oysters. Walk-in/bar; parent of Hermon's. Home turf.

dining.name: Bar Restaurant
dining.notes: Pink-hued, 'strange and fantastic' modern French. Intimate date-night; books up. Sunset Junction, walkable.

dining.name: Sogo Roll Bar
dining.notes: Handroll bar from the Sushi Note team — creative, high-quality fish. Counter seats. Eastside.

dining.name: Lolo Wine Bar
dining.notes: Low-key neighborhood wine bar with a great patio + shareable pasta. Walkable from home.

dining.name: Marco Polo
dining.notes: Outdoor-focused Italian — linguini vongole, gin-arugula cocktails. Patio date-night. Home turf.

dining.name: Clark Street Bakery
dining.notes: Echo Park bakery — caramelized kouign-amann, Nordic breakfast platters. Daytime/casual.

dining.name: Kismet Rotisserie
dining.notes: Casual rotisserie next to Kismet — roast chicken on pita, veg sides. Easy weeknight. Eastside.

dining.name: Jeff's Table
dining.notes: Cult deli hidden behind a liquor store — pastrami, specialty turkey. Lunch. Eastside.

dining.name: Yang's Kitchen
dining.notes: Order-at-counter Taiwanese-Chinese — braised pork rice, beef scallion wraps. SGV-adjacent.

dining.name: Sonmari
dining.notes: Silver Lake handroll spot — inventive DIY rolls (gochujang eel, 'banh mi' albacore). Walkable.

dining.name: Bar Di Bello
dining.notes: Low-lit Milanese-style aperitivo bar — cutlets, branzino, antipasti. Date-night. Home turf.

dining.name: Holbox
dining.notes: Game-changing Mexican seafood stall in Mercado La Paloma — aguachiles, tostadas. Michelin Bib-tier value (confirm). Walk-up.

dining.name: Quarter Sheets
dining.notes: Thick pan-style pizza + great wine list. Bib Gourmand value. Echo Park — walkable from home.

dining.name: Pizzeria Bianco
dining.notes: Chris Bianco's LA outpost (Row DTLA) — among the country's best pizza. Bib Gourmand. Confirm exact address.

dining.name: Sushi Note
dining.notes: Sushi-and-wine bar (team behind Sogo Roll Bar). Valley — a destination, not walkable.

dining.name: Santo
dining.notes: Japanese-Mexican nigiri/handrolls + sake & wine, Sunset Junction. Home turf; next to Bar Seco. (Santō)

dining.name: Bar Seco
dining.notes: Natural wine bar + small plates (CDMX/Madrid/Japan), spills onto Sunset. Walk-in/sidewalk seats. Next to Santo. (aka Seco)

dining.name: Superba
dining.notes: ARI'S ABSOLUTE FAVORITE — food + ambiance, the patio especially (also great inside). Superba Food + Bread, Lincoln Blvd. Westside — worth the drive.

dining.name: L&E Oyster Bar
dining.notes: Silver Lake oyster bar; the upstairs bar is the chill walk-in move. Home turf.

dining.name: Pijja Palace
dining.notes: Indian-Italian sports bar — pizza, pasta, cricket on the TVs. Very popular (hard rez / walk-in bar). Silver Lake, home turf.

dining.name: Night + Market Song
dining.notes: Kris Yenbamroong's fiery northern Thai on Sunset. Walk-in friendly. Home turf.

dining.name: Momed
dining.notes: Mediterranean — mezze, wraps, bowls. Atwater Village (also Beverly Hills). Eastside, easy.

dining.name: Bar Siesta
dining.notes: New Spanish tapas + all-Spanish wine bar (Heather Sperling team). On-taste wine bar, home turf.

dining.name: Atrium
dining.notes: Playful, vaguely-French cooking from Douglas Rankin in the old Malo space, Sunset Junction. New. Home turf.

dining.name: Bowery Bungalow
dining.notes: Modern Mediterranean from George Abou-Daoud in the former Sompun Thai. New, home turf.

dining.name: Frank n Franks
dining.notes: Sandwich spot from a Howlin' Ray's vet. Casual lunch, Chinatown — eastside-adjacent.

events.title: SSRI - Varrio2Varrio (Live); Bloodhound (Live); Taj and Kosmik
events.organizers: The Black Lodge, Yaxteq, Groovers Ball
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Underground Resistance
artist_notes.note: The legendary Detroit techno collective founded by Mike Banks and Jeff Mills — militant, stripped-down techno as political statement; a genuinely mythic name to see billed at a small free Lincoln Heights bar show.

artist_notes.name: Esteban Adame
artist_notes.note: LA-born pianist/producer/DJ who came up in the East LA rave scene of the '90s and was personally recruited into Underground Resistance by Mad Mike Banks in 2004 — fuses jazz, techno and Detroit soul, real pedigree not a tribute act.

artist_notes.name: Nomadico
artist_notes.note: DJ Dex — a UR alum who recorded for the label and now runs the LA label Yaxteq (this event's co-promoter) — gritty, funk-fueled, hard-hitting techno and electro.

artist_notes.name: Kosmik
artist_notes.note: Runs The Black Lodge, the LA techno/esoteric-electronics crew and label co-presenting tonight — dub-leaning, ritualistic techno.

enrichment.curator_note: A genuinely deep Detroit-lineage techno bill dressed up as a free-before-10pm bar night — Esteban Adame and Nomadico both have real Underground Resistance pedigree, and seeing UR itself billed at The Airliner instead of a warehouse or festival stage is the kind of intimate booking you don't get twice.
enrichment.description: Black Lodge, Yaxteq and Groovers Ball present a dub/experimental techno night at The Airliner with Esteban Adame, Nomadico, Bloodhound, Taj, Kosmik, and Underground Resistance, Thu 8/27.

reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +2 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

sounds_like: Elliott Smith's songbook reimagined through jazz-classical arrangement

artist_notes.name: Brad Mehldau
artist_notes.note: One of the most acclaimed jazz pianists of his generation — known for reharmonizing rock/pop songbooks (Radiohead, Nick Drake) through a jazz lens.

artist_notes.name: Chris Thile
artist_notes.note: Mandolin virtuoso, Punch Brothers/Nickel Creek — genre-crossing bluegrass-to-classical musicianship, former host of public radio's 'Live from Here.'

artist_notes.name: Blake Mills
artist_notes.note: In-demand guitarist/producer (Bob Dylan, Alabama Shakes, Perfume Genius) — a go-to for artful, texture-first arrangements.

enrichment.curator_note: This isn't a tribute act — it's Brad Mehldau, Chris Thile and Blake Mills reharmonizing Elliott Smith through a 17-piece chamber orchestra, a one-off arrangement you won't see repeated on a normal tour.
enrichment.description: Pianist Brad Mehldau leads a chamber-orchestra-backed homage to Elliott Smith at the Orpheum, joined by Chris Thile, Blake Mills and John Davis.

artist_notes.note: Portland darkwave/EBM solo project (Conor Knowles) on Artoffact Records — dramatic, mechanized post-industrial post-punk.

artist_notes.name: Sacred Skin
artist_notes.note: LA-based new wave/synthpop/post-punk duo, also on Artoffact Records, touring behind their new LP 'Born In Fire.'

artist_notes.name: Creux Lies
artist_notes.note: Sacramento post-punk/darkwave band with real standing in the current goth revival — self-described 'Californian neo-romantic post-punk,' Cleopatra Records lineage.

enrichment.curator_note: A genuinely deep deathrock/darkwave bill outside the usual lane — Dancing Plague and Sacred Skin both carry real Artoffact Records pedigree and Creux Lies is a legit name in the goth revival, spread across nine acts and two stages at the Regent.

artist_notes.name: Shane Thomas
artist_notes.note: LA producer/DJ, Ace Hotel-residency host of the party blush! — experimental house and techno spliced with reggaeton, dancehall and ballroom edits.

artist_notes.name: Rob Aquino
artist_notes.note: Silver Lake-based promoter (co-runs the monthly Loose party with Bebe) — a fixture of LA's queer underground, mixing techno, house and pop into something weirder than a straight dance set.

artist_notes.name: Banoffee
artist_notes.note: Melbourne-born, LA-based alt-pop producer/singer (Martha Brown) — SOPHIE collaborator and Charli XCX/Empress Of/King Princess associate with deep roots in the queer club circuit; more pop-production pedigree than a straight DJ.

artist_notes.name: Geoboi
artist_notes.note: LA DJ with a thin public bio but a real footprint on the Echo Park/queer-underground circuit (played Sorbet at TBA - Echo Park alongside Shane Thomas) — a dancefloor-first selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Rob Aquino and Shane Thomas both come out of LA's queer-underground crate-digging side, so expect this TBA-location afterhours to run stranger and looser than a standard tech-house night — nobody on the bill is a huge name, but that's kind of the point.
enrichment.description: TBA-location Silver Lake afterhours party (starts midnight) with Shane Thomas, Rob Aquino, Banoffee and Geoboi.

artist_notes.name: Nick Waterhouse

artist_notes.name: Mask Appeal
artist_notes.note: LA post-punk/deathrock trio of scene veterans (members have played in Detroit Cobras, Neighborhood Brats, The Starlite Desperation) — self-titled EP out 2025 on Slouch Records.

enrichment.curator_note: Waterhouse's retro-soul sets are the genuine article, not pastiche, and Mask Appeal isn't a throwaway opener — three LA scene lifers doing sharp old-school post-punk/deathrock. A solid small-room night at Zebulon.

events.title: BAUGRUPPE90, Coffintexts, Trax Unit, Newty
events.detail: Underground giant INCOGNITO celebrates 20 years in the business with a slew of heavy-hitting names who reflect the best of dance music today.
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

sounds_like: Roni Size & Reprazent's 'New Forms' era jungle

artist_notes.name: Roni Size
artist_notes.note: British jungle/drum-and-bass pioneer — Reprazent's Mercury Prize-winning 'New Forms' (1997) is a genre landmark; a genuine dnb legend outside the usual festival circuit.

artist_notes.name: Dieselboy
artist_notes.note: US drum-and-bass mainstay since the '90s, key to breaking the sound stateside (Human Imprint) — breakbeat-heavy, high-energy sets.

artist_notes.name: BAUGRUPPE90
artist_notes.note: German techno duo (Louis Köhler & Paul Vogler) fusing 90s dnb/house/early-2000s-techno textures into a driving, industrial-leaning sound — releases on Sous Music, Steel City Dance Discs, and their own MONTAGE imprint.

artist_notes.name: Coffintexts
artist_notes.note: Miami producer (Alexandra Muggli, Peruvian heritage) blending UK-style techno with bass-heavy, tempo-shifting global rhythms — hardgroove and tribal-house leaning, a rising RA-radar name.

artist_notes.name: Trax Unit
artist_notes.note: LA underground techno duo (Kyle Galindo & Kian Mahroo), Dublab residents who run the local Gyration Station label — stripped-down, analog-grit techno, an actual local scene name rather than a touring import.

enrichment.curator_note: This isn't the vinyl-and-rooftop lane — it's INCOGNITO's 20th-anniversary warehouse weekend, hardgroove techno sliding into full-tilt drum & bass, with actual scene royalty (Roni Size, Dieselboy) instead of the usual local bill. Worth it if you want proof LA's underground rave scene still has teeth.
enrichment.description: INCOGNITO's 20th-anniversary warehouse weekend (TBA location, Sep 4-5) spans hardgroove techno and drum & bass, headlined by dnb legends Roni Size and Dieselboy, with BAUGRUPPE90, Coffintexts, Trax Unit, and residents Newty and WHYS.

events.title: CSW x PACIFIC MODE: Powder [4hr set] and DJ Healthy

sounds_like: eclectic global house/disco selections, viral Boiler Room Tokyo energy

artist_notes.name: Powder
artist_notes.note: Tokyo DJ/producer Momoko 'Moko' Goto — eclectic, colorful disco/house/pop selector known for a widely-circulated Boiler Room Tokyo set.

artist_notes.name: DJ Healthy
artist_notes.note: NY-via-Tokyo selector, founder of the PACIFIC MODE party series — tripped-out house and tech.

enrichment.curator_note: A four-hour open-to-close set from Powder is the draw — she's one of the more genuinely fun, unpredictable selectors on the international circuit, not just a Boiler Room moment.
enrichment.description: PACIFIC MODE hosts a four-hour marathon set from Tokyo DJ Powder with support from DJ Healthy.

events.title: Lights Down Low Feat. Interplanetary Criminal
events.genre: drum and bass, jungle, uk garage
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Interplanetary Criminal
artist_notes.note: Manchester producer riding the UK bassline/2-step revival — skippy, rave-adjacent garage house; a real touring name, not filler.

artist_notes.name: Richie Panic
artist_notes.note: Lights Down Low co-founder (also Frisco Disco, Blow Up) — the LA promoter behind this exact series, known for genre-blurring house/techno bills.

artist_notes.name: Corey Sizemore
artist_notes.note: LDL co-founder and resident, Boiler Room alum — eclectic house-and-techno selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Lights Down Low's warehouse parties are the closest thing LA has to a proper UK rave import, and Interplanetary Criminal's bassline/2-step edits give this one a sharper edge than their usual feel-good house — worth the TBA-location gamble.
enrichment.description: Lights Down Low warehouse party (location TBA) with UK bassline producer Interplanetary Criminal and LDL residents Richie Panic and Corey Sizemore.

events.title: Tokyo Love Song with live performance by Reiko Takahashi
events.detail: City pop / Japanese funk, soul, disco, & synth pop on wax all night long

artist_notes.name: Reiko Takahashi
artist_notes.note: Also performs as Rayko — cut the now-cult 1987 city-pop single 'Sunset Road,' then vanished from music for decades. Only publicly confirmed in early 2026 that she was its singer; now LA-based and performing again. A real appearance from a genuine city-pop ghost story, not a tribute act.

enrichment.curator_note: Reiko Takahashi (Rayko) disappeared after cutting the cult 'Sunset Road' in 1987 and only outed herself as its singer this year — catching her do a live set inside an all-night city-pop/disco vinyl night is the kind of thing that doesn't repeat.
enrichment.description: All-night city pop, Japanese funk/soul and disco vinyl night at Hello Stranger, with a rare live performance from Rayko (Reiko Takahashi), singer of the 1987 cult classic 'Sunset Road.'

events.title: Studio Barnhus Summer Dance Party with Axel Boman, Kornel Kovacs, Nikki Nair
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Axel Boman
artist_notes.note: Swedish producer and Studio Barnhus co-founder — playful, eclectic deep house with a loose, jammy feel (his 'Purple Drank' and marathon festival sets are genre-defining); this is basically his label's home-turf party.

artist_notes.name: Kornél Kovács
artist_notes.note: Studio Barnhus co-founder alongside Axel Boman — bright, melodic, disco-tinged house; one of the most purely fun-first DJs in the European house scene.

artist_notes.name: Nikki Nair
artist_notes.note: Atlanta producer/DJ blending techno, electro, breaks and UK bass into something genre-agnostic and physical — releases on Dirtybird and Lobster Theremin, mentored early by Underground Resistance's Mike Banks.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based selector who co-founded Dig Deeper LA and co-runs Take It Outside — cosmic disco, deep house and left-field selections.

artist_notes.name: Tottie
artist_notes.note: Dublab-affiliated LA radio host and co-founder of SOS Music, a !K7-backed label/platform spotlighting women and non-binary electronic artists.

artist_notes.name: Stacy Christine
artist_notes.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

enrichment.curator_note: Both Studio Barnhus co-founders in one room for an outdoor day party is the label doing exactly what it does best — warm, playful house that doesn't take itself too seriously. Nikki Nair going way outside that lane only makes the bill more interesting.
enrichment.description: Studio Barnhus label showcase at The Bridge, DTLA, with co-founders Axel Boman and Kornél Kovács plus Nikki Nair, Masha Mar, Tottie and Stacy Christine (Sat 9/5, 5pm).

enrichment.curator_note: DJ Sneak going all night on vinyl only is the kind of booking that makes a TBA text worth waiting for — Chicago jacking house from one of its actual architects, not a nostalgia lap.

events.title: Planet X
events.detail: Framework-presented Planet X house/techno night at California Plaza with Ben Sterling, Rafael, and Dean Turnley.

artist_notes.name: Ben Sterling
artist_notes.note: London house/tech-house producer on Diynamic, Crosstown Rebels and Solid Grooves — disco-and-Chicago-house-rooted, championed by Jamie Jones and Patrick Topping.

artist_notes.name: Dean Turnley
artist_notes.note: Melbourne house producer working the Detroit/Chicago lineage — stripped, functional, dancefloor-built; broke out with 'Actin' Tough' hitting #1 on the Beatport chart.

enrichment.curator_note: A proper daytime house/tech-house session at California Plaza from Framework — Ben Sterling's Diynamic/Crosstown Rebels pedigree and Dean Turnley's Chicago-rooted sound make this the closest thing in this batch to an actual sunset-rooftop afternoon.

events.title: Deep in Dis showcase presented by Capsule x Groove Inc

artist_notes.name: Chemtrail Johnny
artist_notes.note: SoCal DJ/producer working in minimal, laid-back house and techno grooves — low profile but a real local scene name.

artist_notes.name: Hazy
artist_notes.note: Recurring Sunday Sessions LA resident — vinyl-only house sets, a regular on the rotation at the series' open-airs.

enrichment.curator_note: Mario Liberti flying in to host his own Deep In Dis showcase is a legitimate deep-techno booking; I couldn't verify CHOíCE, Hazy or Mikeb, so treat this as a solid headliner riding on an unknown undercard.

events.title: Baile World ft Jyoty, Cquestt, Mango & Ginger, Dj Nico

artist_notes.name: Jyoty
artist_notes.note: Indian-Dutch, London-based — Rinse FM resident and Boiler Room regular known for blending baile funk, amapiano, dancehall, jungle and UK garage into one set. Not house/techno, but a legitimately international name for a warehouse booking.

artist_notes.name: Cquestt
artist_notes.note: Courtney Hollinquest — LA native, ex-touring backup dancer turned DJ who founded Baile World in 2020 as an Afro-Latina-led party fusing baile funk, reggaeton, dancehall and Black club music.

artist_notes.name: Mango & Ginger
artist_notes.note: Brazil-by-way-of-LA DJ duo built around baile funk and Afro-diasporic rhythms; best known for NYC's 'Favela Fridays' at SOB's, also play regularly on the LA/Baile World circuit.

enrichment.curator_note: This is warehouse energy but not really the house/techno lane — it's baile funk, dancehall, and global-club selecting. Jyoty's the real draw here (Rinse FM resident, plays the rooms that matter), and Cquestt built Baile World from nothing into a real thing, so the selection will be sharp even off-lane.
enrichment.description: Baile funk, dancehall and global-club warehouse party in DTLA headlined by London's Jyoty, with Baile World founder Cquestt, duo Mango & Ginger, and Dj Nico.

artist_notes.name: Bayymack
artist_notes.note: LA-based artist blending hip-hop, pop and rock (alt-hip-hop/'scene' crossover — collabs with 6arelyhuman, Lil Raven) — not a DJ/producer in the house-techno sense.

enrichment.curator_note: This reads as a Y2K/'scene'-revival night built around Bayymack's hip-hop-pop, not a house or techno booking — fun if you're into that throwback-emo-rap aesthetic, but it's not really your lane despite the late-night 1720 slot.
enrichment.description: Late-night (10pm) Y2K-themed 'scene' party at 1720 in the Arts District with alt-hip-hop artist Bayymack.

events.title: Âme, DJ Tennis, Kaz James - Chinatown Block Party
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

sounds_like: Life and Death's soulful, post-rock-tinged house

artist_notes.name: DJ Tennis
artist_notes.note: Manfredi Romano — Italian scene godfather who founded Life and Death in 2010 (Tale Of Us, Mind Against and Carlita all came up through the label); a globally touring, melodic house/techno selector with real ties to the Innervisions crowd via the Rakastella festival.

artist_notes.name: Kaz James
artist_notes.note: Australian DJ/producer with old-school pedigree — a decade-long Pacha Ibiza residency (Nic Fanciulli's 'We Are The Night') behind him, now making straight-up house that's charted with tracks like 'Not in Love' and 'Footprints.'

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — Italo disco, house and dancefloor edits.

enrichment.curator_note: Âme running an actual outdoor Chinatown block party — not a warehouse pop-up or a festival stage — is exactly the kind of booking worth clearing a Saturday for; DJ Tennis and Masha Mar rounding out the bill only sweetens it.
enrichment.description: Outdoor block party on Gin Ling Way in Chinatown headlined by Innervisions co-founder Âme, with Life and Death's DJ Tennis, plus Kaz James and Masha Mar.

events.title: body wave: Felix Dickinson (UK), Masha Mar, Junior

artist_notes.name: Felix Dickinson
artist_notes.note: UK DJ/producer out of the early-90s free-party scene — deep, chuggy, acid-tinged disco and house; runs Cynic Music, holds residencies at Glastonbury's Block9 and Houghton. A real European-disco-underground name, not a tourist booking.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (Dig Deeper LA, Take It Outside, the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — cosmic disco, deep house, Italo and left-field edits. She's a core-tier artist on your Spotify affinity, worth weighing that in on top of the booking itself.

enrichment.curator_note: Felix Dickinson's chuggy, dub-inflected disco is the UK-import half of this booking, but Masha Mar — one of your heaviest-played artists per your Spotify feedback — running her regular body wave series is the real reason to go; TBA venue is standard for this crew, not a red flag.
enrichment.description: UK disco selector Felix Dickinson headlines the recurring body wave party in DTLA, with Masha Mar and Junior (TBA venue, Sat 9/19).

events.title: FLOAT Rooftop Pool Party feat. Apache [2-8 PM]

enrichment.curator_note: A genuine rooftop-pool day party — Apache isn't a name you'll recognize, but Abracadabra's house lane is legit groove, not brostep-adjacent EDM, and the setting alone (2-8pm, DTLA rooftop) is the Sunset-Sessions kind of afternoon you like.

events.title: Certified Groovers: Gene On Earth in LA

artist_notes.name: Gene On Earth
artist_notes.note: San Francisco-born, Berlin-based DJ/producer (Eugene Albert) — runs the Limousine Dream label; deep-digging extended sets drifting through minimal house, breaks and hazy late-night rollers.

artist_notes.name: Chemtrail Johnny
artist_notes.note: SoCal DJ/producer working in minimal, laid-back house and techno grooves — low profile but a real local scene name.

artist_notes.name: Hazy
artist_notes.note: Recurring Sunday Sessions LA resident — vinyl-only house sets, a regular on the rotation at the series' open-airs.

artist_notes.name: Ian Llorens
artist_notes.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

artist_notes.name: Gilbert0
artist_notes.note: Another Certified Groovers regular — same all-vinyl deep-house lane, secret-location DTLA parties.

enrichment.curator_note: Certified Groovers landing Gene On Earth is a nice get — his Limousine Dream sound is more minimal-and-breaks-leaning than most of the TBA-warehouse bills this month, worth it if you want something a shade weirder than straight house.
enrichment.description: Certified Groovers presents Gene On Earth at a TBA downtown LA location, 10pm.

artist_notes.name: Daphni
artist_notes.note: Dan Snaith's (Caribou) dancefloor-focused alias, running his own Jiaolong label since 2012 — more raw and club-built than his Caribou records, with a strong Afro/global-rhythm bent.

enrichment.curator_note: Daphni isn't a side-project curiosity — it's Caribou's Dan Snaith building tracks specifically for a dancefloor, and he almost never plays full all-night sets; this is the rare chance to hear it stretched out instead of a festival hour.
enrichment.description: Wellness Check presents a full all-night set from Daphni, Dan Snaith's (Caribou) club-facing alias.

events.title: A Club Called Rhonda with DJ Minx, DJ Holographic, Anastazja, Colored Craig
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: DJ Holographic
artist_notes.note: Detroit DJ/producer (Ariel Corley) blending house, disco, Motown, and techno — 2025 debut album 'House In The Dark' leans into Afrofuturism; praised by Carl Craig and The Blessed Madonna, has played Panorama Bar and Smart Bar.

artist_notes.name: Colored Craig
artist_notes.note: LA DJ known for soul/funk/jack-leaning house sets — a regular guest at A Club Called Rhonda over the years.

artist_notes.name: Goddollars
artist_notes.note: LA-born (Loren Granich), co-creator and resident DJ of A Club Called Rhonda — has held down all-vinyl disco sets there with partner Paradise for over a decade.

artist_notes.name: Gay Felony
artist_notes.note: LA DJ/producer (Melody Scallion) — extended vinyl sets ranging from soulful/progressive house to hard house and melodic techno; hosts a Dublab radio show.

artist_notes.name: Anastazja
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ (USC grad) who came up through Soulection Radio, played Boiler Room, and recently supported Keinemusik's Rampa — a credential that tracks with the melodic/Keinemusik lane.

artist_notes.name: DJ Minx
artist_notes.note: Detroit house matriarch, Women on Wax founder — tracked artist; deep, soulful, dancefloor-first selection.

artist_notes.name: A Club Called Rhonda
artist_notes.note: LA's own queer disco/house institution (Loren Granic & Gregory Alexander) — the closest thing on this bill to the rooftop-groove lane, all disco edits and drag-flecked chaos rather than a band.

enrichment.curator_note: A Club Called Rhonda is one of the last real queer dance institutions left in LA, and stacking Detroit's DJ Holographic next to their own deep bench of residents (Goddollars, Gay Felony, Colored Craig) plus DJ Minx makes this one of the stronger bills on the whole calendar, not just a queer-night box to check.
enrichment.description: Long-running LA queer club night A Club Called Rhonda at Los Globos, with Detroit house veterans DJ Minx and DJ Holographic plus a deep bill of LA residents.

enrichment.curator_note: An open-to-close Rich Medina set billed explicitly as house/rare-groove/garage is exactly the deep-crate education worth clearing a whole Saturday night for at a tiki bar like High Tide.

events.title: Jimi Jules (Open To Close)
events.detail: Swiss house/disco selector Jimi Jules plays a rare open-to-close set at Gin Ling Way in Chinatown — European-leaning, fabric-style booking.

artist_notes.name: Jimi Jules
artist_notes.note: Zurich-born, Berlin-based (longtime Watergate resident) house producer now signed to Innervisions — jazzy, soulful, musician's-ear house that broke through via 2014's Defected hit 'Pushing On.'

enrichment.curator_note: An open-to-close booking from an Innervisions/Watergate name is the kind of set where the arc matters more than any single hour — Gin Ling Way's alley setting should suit his deeper, jazzier register.

events.title: If You Know You Know with DJ Masda (CABARET Recordings)

artist_notes.name: DJ Masda
artist_notes.note: Japan-born, Berlin-based co-founder of CABARET Recordings — vinyl digger since the '90s pulling from early techno, futurist electro and playful house; RA Podcast/Dimensions pedigree, has played LA's Pattern Bar before.

artist_notes.name: Mesmé
artist_notes.note: LA DJ/producer (debut EP on Mall Grab's Steel City Dance Discs) — vinyl-heavy blends of moody acid, electro, house and trip-hop; Into the Woods and Dublab resident, Boiler Room 2021.

artist_notes.name: Etari
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Alixandria Andre) — hypnotic house and broken-beat selector who's played Lights Down Low and Incognito and a HÖR Berlin set; Yellow Island Records.

artist_notes.name: Connor Mikami
artist_notes.note: Founder of If You Know You Know, the LA party/label series this event IS — longtime local selector working vintage breaks, electro and club records.

artist_notes.name: Chemtrail Johnny
artist_notes.note: SoCal DJ/producer working in minimal, laid-back house and techno grooves — low profile but a real local scene name.

enrichment.curator_note: Connor Mikami's own IYKYK series flying in DJ Masda's Tokyo-to-Berlin house/techno digging, but the real story is the bench underneath him — Mesmé and Etari are both legit names on their own nights. TBA spot means expect a real underground room, not a listed venue.

events.title: Boiler Room: LA | Sunday
reasons: +4 event card (+3 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Floorplan
artist_notes.note: Robert Hood & daughter Lyric Hood — Detroit techno royalty (M-Plant) turned deep, gospel-inflected house. 'Baby Baby' fills a floor for a reason.

artist_notes.name: HoneyLuv
artist_notes.note: Cleveland-born, ex-Navy — one of the biggest tech-house breakouts of the last few years; soulful, groovy end of the genre, runs her own 4 Tha Luv label.

artist_notes.name: Hannah Laing
artist_notes.note: Dundee DJ, ex-dental technician turned fast-rising UK name — high-energy trance and hard house, runs the doof label and just launched her own festival.

artist_notes.name: Coco & Breezy
artist_notes.note: Twin sisters (also the eyewear-brand founders) turned house/dance DJ duo — danceable, R&B-tinged, more crossover-pop energy than underground.

artist_notes.name: STRAWBRY
artist_notes.note: LA underground fixture (South Florida-raised) — breaks-and-house sets, runs the STUDIO5400 party series.

artist_notes.name: Vieze Asbak
artist_notes.note: Dutch 'memecore'/troll-rave artist out of Amsterdam's Pestcore Collectief — hard-dance-adjacent chaos, not clean house or techno. A sign this bill gets weird in spots.

artist_notes.name: Jazzy (IRL)
artist_notes.note: Couldn't pin down a confident bio for this one — flagging as unverified rather than guessing.

enrichment.curator_note: Boiler Room's Sunday day party stacks Floorplan's gospel house and HoneyLuv's tech-house heat against Hannah Laing's hard-house hype and a Dutch memecore act, with several names even RA barely has bios for — genuinely one of the most eclectic single-day bills on the radar, go in expecting variety over consistency.
enrichment.description: Boiler Room's LA day party (venue TBA) — a 14-act, multi-genre bill headlined by Floorplan, HoneyLuv, and Hannah Laing.

events.detail: The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.Adapted from S.E. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation."In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self- discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging…and the realization that there is still “lots of good in the world.”

sounds_like: deep, soulful West Coast house lineage
the sound that built LA's dance scene

artist_notes.name: Marques Wyatt
artist_notes.note: West Coast deep-house legend — ran LA's long-running Deep party/residency from the late '90s into the 2010s, credited with helping put LA's dance scene on the map alongside NYC and Miami.

artist_notes.name: Doc Martin
artist_notes.note: West Coast house pioneer, moved SF to LA in the early '90s and founded the long-running Sublevel label/party (25 years deep in 2026) — deep, tribal, acid-inflected house from a genuine scene elder.

artist_notes.name: David Harness
artist_notes.note: Bay Area deep-house DJ/producer/remixer (credits with Mary J. Blige, Alicia Keys) — soulful, classic house across Coachella, Glastonbury and beyond.

artist_notes.name: Big Cee

events.title: Bonnie Raitt: Live 2026 with Special Guest Jon Cleary
lineup: Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen
events.detail: Bluesy singer/songwriter Bonnie Raitt has worked long and hard for her multiple Grammy Awards, hit singles and chart-topping records. Since her 1971 eponymous debut, the California-born performer and long-time activist has steadily maintained a music career, albeit with definite peaks and valleys. The red-headed songstress, one of the only women of her time to play guitar using the bottleneck technique, unleashed seven albums in just nine years, though her big commercial break came with her 10th studio set, 1989’s “Nick of Time.” That 11-track collection, produced by Don Was, earned three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. Not only has the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer tackled multiple U.S. tours and international runs, but she’s also a frequent participant in events of social activism, such as Farm Aid and Amnesty International concerts. Raitt’s 16th full-length album and most recent studio release, “Slipstream,” hit retailers in 2012. Not only did ticket sales for the support tour soar, but Raitt also landed the best-selling blues album of the year and took home the Grammy for Best Americana Album.

reasons: +3 event card (+1 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

sounds_like: hypnotic, dense techno in the Inner Tension/SXTCY mold

artist_notes.name: Anastasia Giovani
artist_notes.note: LA underground techno regular — SXTCY resident known for dark, raw, propulsive sets; also runs VSCRL, a modular/vinyl/noise-leaning event series.

artist_notes.name: Blazej Malinowski
artist_notes.note: Polish, Berlin-based techno producer — founder of the Inner Tension label, deep and hypnotic productions on Semantica and Silent Season.

artist_notes.name: Kameliia
artist_notes.note: Oslo-based techno DJ (Bulgarian-born) — self-described 'mental techno,' driving and atmospheric, releases on Token and SK_eleven; has played Berghain, Fold and Berlin Atonal.

artist_notes.name: Secus
artist_notes.note: LA techno producer (Matt Salamone) — half of Motionen, co-founder of label Ascetic Limited; jazz/metal-informed, hard and agitated techno.

enrichment.curator_note: A legit deep-techno afterhours booking — Berlin's Blazej Malinowski and Oslo's Kameliia flying in alongside LA's own Anastasia Giovani and Secus for a 5am TBA start. Hypnotic, dense end of the spectrum, not big-room — worth it only if you're actually built for a real after-hours.

events.title: The Who's Tommy (Touring)
events.detail: In 1969, The Who created a rock opera that changed the course of music history. And now,it’s back in a dazzling all-new production that feels more relevant than ever.Myth and spectacle combine in this fresh reinvention that includes the unforgettable anthems “I’m Free,” “See Me, Feel Me,” “Sensation” and “Pinball Wizard.” After witnessing his father shoot his rival, the young Tommy Walker is lost in the universe, endlessly and obsessively staring into the mirror. An innate knack for pinball catapults him from reticent adolescent to celebrity savior. Tony Award-winning composer Pete Townshend and Tony Award-winning original director Des McAnuff find powerful resonance reexamining this classic story for today.

events.title: SNEAK'S BIRTHDAY BEATS 2026
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Derrick Carter
artist_notes.note: Chicago house legend since the late-'80s Warehouse/Muzic Box lineage — co-runs Classic Music Company with Luke Solomon; funky, genre-agnostic, unmistakable house selection still headlining at this level.

artist_notes.name: DJ Sneak
artist_notes.note: Chicago house OG ('the Turntable Terrorist') — jacking, sample-heavy garage-house going back to the early-'90s Cajmere/Relief era, still DJing at that level today.

artist_notes.name: DJ Heather
artist_notes.note: Chicago house DJ, co-founder of the pioneering all-female Superjane crew (with DJ Colette, Dayhota, Lady D) — soulful, genre-blurring sets rooted in Gramaphone Records digging.

artist_notes.name: H-Foundation
artist_notes.note: San Diego duo (Hipp-E & Halo) — dub-inflected deep/tech-house with a Fabric London residency and a Chemical Brothers remix credit to their name; not a frequent LA booking.

artist_notes.name: Hector Moralez
artist_notes.note: Oakland-raised, now LA-based house DJ/producer (Minority Music, The Factory labels) — Chicago/Detroit-rooted, soul-deep selections; a regular in Sneak's LA circle.

artist_notes.name: J-Dub
artist_notes.note: Chicago-bred new-school house DJ and frequent DJ Sneak collaborator on the LA circuit (CHI♡LA, Certified Groovers) — funky, percussive, seamless-blend style.

artist_notes.name: Juliet Mendoza
artist_notes.note: LA-native house DJ and dancer — founder/resident of Jill's House (Jackin Jills), a Defected 'Unsung Heroes' alum; melodic, soulful, deep house rooted in the city's Black/Latin house dance lineage.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — Italo disco, house and dancefloor edits.

artist_notes.name: Ian Llorens
artist_notes.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

artist_notes.name: Stacy Christine
artist_notes.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

artist_notes.name: John Tejada
artist_notes.note: Vienna-born, LA-based since childhood — Palette Recordings founder and a fixture of musical, melodic techno/deep house since the mid-90s (Kompakt, Pokerflat, Cocoon). Real underground pedigree headlining his own night.

artist_notes.name: Heidi Lawden
artist_notes.note: LA-via-London selector who cut her teeth in the '90s UK queer rave scene — house/techno/disco marathon sets (an 8-hour solo warehouse set till 8am) and a longtime DJ Harvey tour collaborator/muse. Also on the Defected boardwalk afterparty this batch.

artist_notes.name: Dj Kerry
artist_notes.note: LA DJ since 2005, longtime Dublab radio host and founder of The Basement, a membership-based party rooted in Paradise Garage/West Coast warehouse tradition.

enrichment.curator_note: Sneak's birthday parties are always deep, but pulling Derrick Carter, DJ Heather and H-Foundation back into the same room is a real reunion of the Chicago class that built this sound — worth clearing the whole afternoon for, even with the venue still a mystery.
enrichment.description: DJ Sneak's annual birthday day-party (TBA DTLA-area location, Sat 11/14, 4pm) stacks Chicago house legends Derrick Carter, DJ Heather and H-Foundation with LA scene regulars Hector Moralez, J-Dub, Juliet Mendoza, Masha Mar, Ian Llorens and Stacy Christine.
